text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- A 13-member hit squad formed by an organised crime boss is arrested by Istanbul police.
- The government will end a compulsory savings scheme and start paying back the 630 trillion lira gathered in the fund over the years.
MILLIYET
- The speaker of parliament calls for a delay in parliament's summer break so that the new government can make a start on its policies.
- Deputy Prime Minister Ismet Sezgin says 24 jailed editors will be released.
HURRIYET
- The government's three priorities are eight-year compulsory education, an amnesty for journalists and a census.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz promises to accelerate the privatisation process.
YENI YUZYIL

- A former deputy police intelligence chief tells a parliamentary commission investigating a security scandal that an intelligence agent was responsible for starting 1995 riots in a poor district of Istanbul.
RADIKAL
- A Turkish prosecutor investigating former prime minister Tansu Ciller's personal wealth is preparing to ask the United States for information on her assets there.
- Petroleum product prices rise by 15 to 32 percent.
CUMHURIYET
- Yilmaz says there will be no amnesty for tax debtors.
DUNYA
- Turkey and the European Union have clashed over EU plans to finance non-governmental organisations without the involvement of the state.
ZAMAN
- Wrestler Ahmet Tasci won the traditional grease wrestling championship for the second time.
